newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen police besiege abductors of seven Germans.
newsitem.headline: Yemen police besiege abductors of seven Germans.

text.p: Security forces laid siege to parts of southeastern Yemen on Thursday to help free seven German tourists seized by local tribesmen, officials said.

The men were kidnapped on Monday while riding motorcycles through the Wadi al-Dabaat area between Mahra and Hadramaut provinces, Yemeni officials said on Wednesday. Their local travel agency reported their abduction on Tuesday.
"Security forces are surrounding parts of the wadi area to tighten the noose on the kidnappers to try and win the freedom of the hostages," one Yemeni official told Reuters.
"We will deal wisely, but at the same time firmly, with the abductors to get the hostages out safely," he said.
The official and others gave no further details and the German embassy declined comment.

Official sources had said the kidnappers, all local tribesmen, wanted to put pressure on the government to bring to justice an alleged Yemeni swindler who sold them smuggled cars brought in from Saudi Arabia and other Gulf states.

"The man was held by local authorities for 17 days before disappearing," one source told Reuters. "They are trying to put pressure on the government to bring him to justice and to have their money returned."
They said the abductors had telephoned local authorities to demand 12 million marks ($7 million) ransom for their release.
"It seems they are calculating a $1 million ransom per head," one official in Sanaa said.
But Hadramaut police chief Ali Nasser Lakhshaa denied the kidnappers were demanding a ransom.
Hadramaut is 770 km (480 miles) east of Sanaa, close to the border with Oman.
Yemeni tribes with grievances against the government or foreign oil firms have kidnapped scores of tourists, diplomats or other foreigners in recent years to use as bargaining chips.
An American diplomat and a Saudi ambassador have been among the kidnap victims. There have been no reported casualties from the abductions and all of the hostages have been released unharmed.
Some were rescued by security forces, others were set free.
An American oil engineer held for 16 days by a Yemeni mountain tribe was released on February 26.

His kidnappers had demanded compensation of $2 million or the return of a piece of land in Sanaa which they said was given to one of their tribal leaders. It was not clear whether their demands were met in return for the engineer's release.
